components.name: alacritty_terminal
components.role: VT emulator: grid, colours, cursor, modes, alternate screen and scrollback for the integrated terminal
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core. Only the Term/Grid/parser surface is used; the crate's own tty, event_loop and thread modules are unused because the PTY stays with portable-pty. Replaces the vt100 emulator and the handwritten DECSCUSR tracker built on vte.

version.reason: Current stable release; MSRV 1.85 matches the project. Same emulator that backs Alacritty and Zed, and it re-exports the vte 0.15 the core already resolved.

maintenance.statusAtReview: Official Alacritty project; emulator in production use for years

runtimeSecurity.notes: The crate ships a tty module capable of spawning processes, but Kinein never calls it; sessions are created by portable-pty and only raw bytes reach the emulator.

scopeControls: Only Term, Grid and the ANSI Processor are used; tty/event_loop/thread stay unused
VoidListener: the core polls the grid instead of consuming emulator events
Scrollback bounded by Config::scrolling_history (5000 lines)
No CLI name, prompt text or user content is interpreted
Grid, modes and cursor share one mutex snapshot per frame
event.terminal.render contract unchanged by the swap
verification: Contract preserved: cursor/modes/scrollback/spans identical in the typed event

components.name: exmex
components.role: Expression parser and evaluator for the `sim` domain: parses the formula the user types, reports which variables it uses, and evaluates it per integration step
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core, behind the `sim` domain. `var_names()` feeds the concept check that runs on every keystroke; `eval()` runs the integration step. The evaluation vector is assembled from the user's explicit variable binding, never from the crate's positional order.

version.reason: Current release (2026-05-23) and the only MAINTAINED expression evaluator that passes this repository's deny.toml. MSRV 1.80.1 is below the workspace 1.85. The `partial` feature (partial derivatives) adds no dependency: it is `partial = []`.

license.source: Published crate manifest, read from the vendored source on 2026-09-05

maintenance.statusAtReview: Active: latest release 2026-05-23. Compared against five alternatives; evalexpr relicensed MIT -> AGPL-3.0-only at v12.0.0 (2024-10-17) and is rejected, mexprp is rejected for LGPL-3.0-or-later reaching in through rug/gmp-mpfr-sys, and fasteval/meval/rsc pass the licence gate but last shipped in 2020/2018/2024.

runtimeSecurity.notes: Measured on 2026-09-05 by grepping the vendored src/: zero occurrences of std::net, std::process, std::fs, std::env, `unsafe`, or any HTTP client. It is pure computation over f64. Four behavioural traps were found by exercising it and are recorded in ADR-0006: alphabetical variable order (defused by the explicit binding in arquitetura/34 5.0), lowercase `pi` parsed as a free variable, division by zero yielding silent inf/NaN, and parser error text containing a raw pointer address, which the IDE never forwards to the screen.

cost.notes: Measured against this workspace, not an empty project: its six transitive dependencies (regex, regex-automata, regex-syntax, aho-corasick, memchr, smallvec) were already present, so only exmex itself is new. An isolated measurement reports +7 and does not apply here.

components.verification: cargo deny check (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) green on the real workspace with the crate in place, 2026-09-05

components.name: rustix
components.role: Safe `access(2)` for the `serial` domain: tells whether the user can read and write a serial device node WITHOUT opening it (opening asserts DTR/RTS on most USB-UART bridges and resets the board)
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core, one call site in serial.rs (`rustix::fs::access`). Declared with default-features = false and features ["std", "fs"]. Chosen over a stat()-based check because access(2) honours POSIX ACLs, which is how udev's TAG+="uaccess" grants the seat user access without any group; a mode-bit heuristic would report `root:dialout 0660` as writable for a user outside dialout, or as denied for a user covered by the ACL.

version.reason: Already resolved at 1.1.4 in Cargo.lock as a transitive dependency of portable-pty (rustix-openpty) and alacritty_terminal (polling) before this adoption; declaring it directly adds no crate and no second version.

license.spdx: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
license.source: crates.io version metadata for 1.1.4, read on 2026-09-11; MIT and Apache-2.0 are already in deny.toml

maintenance.statusAtReview: Active: Bytecode Alliance project, latest release 2026-02-22; it is the syscall layer under std-adjacent crates such as tempfile and the async-io stack.

runtimeSecurity.notes: It is a thin wrapper over Linux syscalls (raw syscalls or libc, chosen by the crate's backend); the `unsafe` lives inside it and none in this repository (#![forbid(unsafe_code)] stays). Kinein calls only fs::access, which reads nothing and writes nothing.

cost.notes: Measured with `cargo tree -i rustix` on 2026-09-11: the crate was already in the graph via polling and rustix-openpty; the direct declaration only widens its feature set by `fs`.

components.verification: cargo deny check (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) green on the real workspace with the crate declared, 2026-09-11; the `serial` tests exercise access() against 0o000, 0o060 and 0o600 nodes

components.name: SymPy
components.role: Exactness ORACLE for the `sim` domain: solves the differential equation the user actually typed, so the `exato` column stops answering for the concept's canonical equation
components.integration: External process, ORCHESTRATED and never linked — the same boundary as GDB. The core spawns `python3 -c <program>` with a JSON request on stdin and reads one JSON line back; the program is embedded in `crates/kinein-core/src/sim/oraculo.rs`. ONE trip per FORMULA, never per point: SymPy returns the closed form and `exmex` evaluates the whole trail. Absent, it degrades in the open: the `exato` column keeps the concept's answer and the screen says so (`SimAccuracySource`).

version.pin: NOT pinned, and it must not be: this is a tool on the USER's machine, like clangd or GDB. The IDE detects it and says when it is missing; it never installs it.
version.reason: Optional dependency. Measured on 2026-09-06 and again on 2026-09-10: it is ABSENT on the author's machine, which is exactly why the degraded path is the one the product ships with by default.

license.source: Fedora 44 package metadata for python3-sympy, read on 2026-09-06 (roadmaps/31 §19.3.1). Not linked, so no license obligation propagates to the binary either way.

maintenance.statusAtReview: Active: 1.14.0 is the current release, packaged by every major distribution. No alternative was adopted — the CAS written in Rust (symbolica) is source-available with proprietary terms and is FORBIDDEN here (roadmaps/31 §12.3, the Pylance category); Maxima was measured and refused as a narrator (§13.1, upstream marked the step-by-step request won't fix).

components.runtimeSecurity: Runs as a child process with stdin/stdout piped and stderr discarded, with a 5-second ceiling and a kill on expiry. It receives only the formula the user typed plus numeric parameters — never a file path, never the workspace. Its answer is NEVER trusted as code: it goes through a gate that requires `exmex` to parse it and its only free variable to be `t`, which is what stops the silent `pi` trap measured in §19.3.4.
components.cost: 425-506 ms per run measured end to end on 2026-09-10, of which ~200 ms is `import sympy`. Paid once per explicit 'Integrar', never per keystroke.
components.verification: crates/kinein-core/src/tests/sim_oraculo.rs — 9 tests against a FAKE python3 (scripts/fake_sympy_oracle.py) that records the request it received. Five mutations prove the gates. Exercised against the real binary and real SymPy on 2026-09-10 (roadmaps/40 §7.3).
